subtitle: Inverted Phaser
tagline: Subtracts an all-pass-shifted copy from the dry signal for deep, hard-edged cancellation notches that move, park, or break apart.

body.lead: A classic phaser adds a phase-shifted copy to the dry signal. TB Inverted Phaser subtracts that copy instead, producing deep cancellation notches with hard, defined edges.

body.p: You choose how many notches are cut, where they sit, how far apart they are, and how they move. Amount and Mix are independent, so the sound can range from structured motion to an exposed, strongly coloured residue. It works especially well on pads, sustained chords, and harmonic material.

ul: Cascade of up to 12 all-pass stages, subtracted from the dry signal
CENTER, STAGE COUNT, and SPACING define the notch pattern
Five LFO shapes plus JITTER for random drift
RANGE 0% parks the notches as a fixed comb
Independent AMOUNT and MIX, plus OUTPUT trim
Display of the input spectrum and the phase response together
Thirteen factory presets in three banks, with undo and redo

note.title: About this manual
text: This manual describes TB Inverted Phaser 3.0.0 for Windows (VST3). The current macOS build is version 1.0.2 and may differ from the descriptions here.

ol: Insert TB Inverted Phaser on a pad, chord, or other sustained sound. The defaults are `CENTER` 720 Hz, `RATE` 0.35 Hz, `RANGE` 70%, `STAGE COUNT` 6, `SPACING` 35%, `FEEDBACK` 28%, `AMOUNT` 65%, `MIX` 100%.
Move `CENTER` {{3}} to the part of the sound you want to hollow out.
Set the speed with `RATE` and the travel with `RANGE` {{7}}.
Choose how many notches with `STAGE COUNT` {{6}} and how far apart they are with `SPACING` {{8}}.
Raise `FEEDBACK` {{9}} for sharper, more resonant notch edges.
Balance `AMOUNT` {{10}} and `MIX` {{11}}, then match the level with `OUTPUT` {{12}}.

rows: The frequency the notch pattern is built around. Move it to choose which part of the sound is hollowed out.
How fast the notches travel. Low values drift; high values warble.
Sine, Triangle, Ramp Up, Ramp Down, Square · Sine
The shape of the movement. Sine and Triangle glide, Ramp restarts, and Square jumps between two positions.
Random drift added on top of the movement. Small amounts loosen the motion; large amounts break it up.
How many notches are cut. More stages give a denser, more metallic cancellation.
How far the notches travel from CENTER. At 0% they stay parked and act as a fixed comb.
The distance between notches in octaves. Narrow is tight and resonant; wide spreads across the spectrum.
Returns the shifted copy into the cascade. Raises resonance and sharpens the notch edges.
How much of the phase-shifted copy is subtracted from the dry signal. This is the depth of the cancellation.
Level of the untouched dry signal that AMOUNT is subtracted from. Lower it to leave mostly the cancelled residue.
Final level trim, for matching loudness against bypass.

warn.text: Because the effect works by cancellation, it can remove parts of the sound and change the level. Large FEEDBACK and RANGE settings are worth checking in mono.

body.p: Factory presets are grouped in three banks: Moving Notch, Fixed Comb, and Broken. Selecting a preset replaces every value in a single undo step. Save writes every current value to a .tbipreset file in your Documents folder. Undo steps back through parameter and preset changes; Redo steps forward again.

Factory presets: **Init**, **Pad Drift**, **Slow Orbit**, **Wide Vortex**, **Fast Warble**, **Ramp Sweeper**, **Thin Air**, **Hollow Glass**, **Static Teeth**, **Metal Rail**, **Square Jolt**, **Broken Motion**, and **Ghost Cancel**.
Starting points for common jobs. Adjust them by ear.

recipes.title: Slow pad motion
recipes.use: Gentle, evolving movement on sustained chords.
steps: Place CENTER in the busiest part of the pad.
Lower MIX slightly if the result is too hollow.

recipes.title: Fixed metallic comb
recipes.use: A static, resonant colour instead of movement.
steps: Sweep CENTER by hand to tune the comb to the sound.

recipes.title: Stepped rhythmic jumps
recipes.use: Movement that switches between two positions.
settings: Set by ear against the groove
steps: RATE is in hertz; adjust it to match the music.

recipes.title: Exposed residue
recipes.use: An extreme, filtered texture made from what is cancelled.
steps: Raise OUTPUT to make up the level.

rows: The sound became thin or quiet.
That is the cancellation. Lower AMOUNT, or raise OUTPUT to match the bypassed level.
RANGE is at 0%, which parks them as a fixed comb. Raise RANGE.
The effect is too harsh or resonant.
Raise AMOUNT, add stages, or move CENTER to a busier part of the sound.
